title: US10621973B1 — Sub-vocal speech recognition apparatus and method
what_they_did: A headset worn over the ear carries EMG electrodes and an IMU in contact with the skin over the neck, under the chin and behind the ear; sub-vocal speech is recorded, amplified, filtered and windowed into multi-millisecond frames for recognition.
useful_for_us: The closest claimed combination of chin plus neck EMG with a jaw IMU; active to 2038, so our hidden-jaw device needs a different site set or a design-around rather than the same chin/neck/behind-ear triad.

title: US8082149B2 — Methods and apparatuses for myoelectric-based speech processing
what_they_did: Captures a myoelectric signal from a user with at least one electrode, amplifies, filters and digitises it, then processes the signal for speech; assigned to Biosensic LLC with Tanja Schultz as inventor.
useful_for_us: The foundational EMG-speech patent by the field's best-known group; its 45-member family includes continuations US11222185B2 and US11972227B2, so the basic electrode-plus-processing claim stays alive across many years.

title: US12505842B2 — Devices, systems, and methods for personal speech recognition and replacement
what_they_did: A personal device with a cutaneous sensor unit detects surface EMG from articulatory muscles and wirelessly sends it to a computing device that recognises silent speech, aimed at laryngectomy and voice-rest patients.
useful_for_us: Clinical sEMG silent-speech claim naming articulatory muscles and a wearable cutaneous unit; useful evidence that chin/neck sEMG can be framed as voice restoration and that a small sensor unit is patentable.

title: US12400473B2 — Wearable facial movement tracking devices
what_they_did: Head-mounted or neck-mounted wearables with cameras or acoustic sensors learn skin-deformation and facial-feature patterns to reconstruct facial expressions and movements.
useful_for_us: The optical/acoustic competitor route to EMG: it proves facial tracking from a head-worn device but needs camera line of sight and raises the occlusion and privacy problems our hidden EMG device avoids.

title: US11216069B2 — Systems and methods for improved speech recognition using neuromuscular information
what_they_did: Multiple neuromuscular sensors on one or more wearables continuously record neuromuscular signals, and a trained inference model takes audio plus the neuromuscular signals (or signals derived from them) and determines text.
useful_for_us: The core Meta/CTRL-labs claim combining neuromuscular sensing with audio for speech recognition; broad and active to 2038, so it belongs at the top of any freedom-to-operate watch list for a neuromuscular wearable.

title: US11036302B1 — Wearable devices and methods for improved speech recognition
what_they_did: Wearable-device variants of the Meta neuromuscular speech system: sensors record neuromuscular signals, models determine text, with embodiments covering the wearable housing and sensor arrangement.
useful_for_us: Shows Meta claimed the wearable hardware separately from the signal-processing method; a reminder that both the sensor housing and the decoding pipeline can be separately claimed.

title: US12579768B2 — Wearable electronic devices, extended reality systems including neuromuscular sensors, and methods for generating text from speech input
what_they_did: Neuromuscular sensors on a wearable sense signals, and processors generate text and XR interactions from the sensed neuromuscular data.
useful_for_us: A late Meta grant in the same family that extends the claims into extended-reality use; shows how a single neuromotor portfolio is kept alive with continuation grants.

title: US12154572B2 — Identifying silent speech using recorded speech
what_they_did: Signals representing pre-vocalisation facial skin micromovements are received in a first time period and signals representing sounds in a succeeding period, and the micromovements are interpreted using the recorded speech.
useful_for_us: The Q (Cue) optical-micromovement approach that self-supervises on recorded speech to decode silent speech; a 101-member family and the technology behind Apple's acquisition, so it is a major adjacent claim space.

title: US12482449B2 — Systems and methods for using silent speech in a user interaction system
what_they_did: A speech input device wearable on the user receives an electronic signal indicative of the user's speech-muscle activation patterns, including EMG data, and uses it in a user-interaction system with a knowledge system.
useful_for_us: Wispr AI's granted claim explicitly covers a wearable that reads speech-muscle activation EMG; the 15-member family is active, so check it before claiming an EMG silent-speech wearable.

title: US10678502B2 — Systems and methods for in-ear control of remote devices
what_they_did: An in-ear device microphone receives audio, a speech-recognition technique determines a command, and a voice-recognition technique identifies the wearer before controlling remote devices.
useful_for_us: In-ear form-factor precedent for command input; it is acoustic rather than silent, so it does not block ear-canal deformation or EMG sensing but shows the earbud interaction claim pattern.

title: US11683632B2 — Automatic speech recognition triggering system
what_they_did: An ASR triggering system uses a microphone plus an accelerometer worn in the ear canal to generate a non-acoustic bone-conduction signal that triggers speech recognition.
useful_for_us: Apple's ear-canal accelerometer claim, with a three-grant family (US10313782B2, US11102568B2, US11683632B2); relevant to any in-ear or behind-ear vibration sensor on our device.

title: US9779758B2 — Augmenting speech segmentation and recognition using head-mounted vibration and/or motion sensors
what_they_did: Audio in the speech band from a microphone is combined with vibration data from a non-microphone sensor on a head-mountable device to decide whether and when the speaker is speaking.
useful_for_us: Head-mounted vibration and motion sensing for speech segmentation; a Google claim that covers using a second, non-acoustic sensor to gate speech, which is how a jaw-mounted sensor is likely to be used.

title: US10679644B2 — Production of speech based on whispered speech and silent speech
what_they_did: Multiple sensors capture low-amplitude whispered or silent speech, computing devices analyse the sensor data, map it to speech, and transmit amplified speech to a remote communication device.
useful_for_us: IBM claims a multi-sensor silent/whispered speech pipeline end to end; its continuation US10529355B2 shows the sensor-fusion claim was filed twice, so the concept is well covered.

title: US11397799B2 — User authentication by subvocalization of melody singing
what_they_did: A computing device acquires a representation of a melody subvocalised by the user and authenticates the user when it matches a reference melody closely enough.
useful_for_us: An authentication use of subvocalisation rather than speech decoding; useful as a secondary claim target if our jaw device also supports an unlock gesture, and it shows subvocal signals are treated as biometrics.

title: US11154232B2 — Mechano-acoustic sensing devices and methods
what_they_did: A soft, conformal device records mechano-acoustic signals from skin almost anywhere on the body and can add electrophysiological recording for multimodal operation.
useful_for_us: The soft-conformal materials route (Rogers group) for picking up throat and jaw vibration; useful if the hidden device records mechano-acoustic rather than purely electrical signals.

title: US8242880B2 — Tongue operated magnetic sensor systems and methods
what_they_did: A magnetic tracer unit is placed on the tongue and a sensor system near the mouth tracks the tracer's position, enabling assistive control.
useful_for_us: Intraoral magnetic tracking is a fully different sensing modality from EMG and is now INACTIVE, so the concept is relatively free to use, but it needs a tracer on the tongue, which is not hidden.

title: US9911358B2 — Wireless real-time tongue tracking for speech impairment diagnosis, speech therapy with audiovisual biofeedback, and silent speech interface
what_they_did: A small magnetic tracer on the tongue plus an array of magnetic sensors around the mouth localises the tongue with sub-millimetre precision and fuses that with acoustic, video and airflow data in a silent-speech interface.
useful_for_us: Georgia Tech explicitly claimed a silent-speech-interface use of tongue tracking; now INACTIVE, which makes it useful prior art and a design dead-end requiring a tongue tracer rather than hidden jaw sensing.

title: US7082395B2 — Signal injection coupling into the human vocal tract for robust audible and inaudible voice recognition
what_they_did: Artificial excitation is injected into the human vocal tract to enhance or replace natural excitation, adding spectral, temporal or phase data so that audible or inaudible mouthed/whispered speech is recognised more robustly.
useful_for_us: An early subvocal approach that is now EXPIRED; it is direct evidence that external excitation of the vocal tract was tried and did not become a product, which is a dead-end warning for hardware-heavy silent-speech schemes.

title: CN113288183B — Silent speech recognition based on facial-neck surface electromyography
what_they_did: Surface EMG from a high-density electrode array and from sparse discrete electrodes is preprocessed and turned into high-density and channel-sparse sEMG image sets; a source-domain network is trained and transfer learning calibrates it on the target domain so discrete-electrode silent words can be classified.
useful_for_us: This is essentially our problem statement from USTC: high-density arrays are used to train, few discrete electrodes are used to wear, and transfer learning handles electrode shift and cross-user variation; active to 2041.

title: CN114863912A — Silent voice decoding method based on surface electromyogram signals
what_they_did: Silent-speech sEMG data is collected and featurised into a training set, a Transformer-based decoding network is built and trained, and the optimised network decodes silent speech.
useful_for_us: The same USTC group moved from a CNN-style classifier to a Transformer decoder, which is the architecture direction we should copy for small sEMG vocabularies.

title: CN114822541A — Silent speech recognition method and system based on back translation
what_they_did: Silent-state surface EMG is collected, preprocessed and featurised, fed to an SAEM model, and back-translation is used to expand or regularise the silent-speech recognition.
useful_for_us: A concrete data-augmentation recipe (back-translation) from the Chinese defence lab for the small-corpus problem that will also limit our one-user jaw dataset.

title: CN112151030B — Multimodal speech recognition method and apparatus for complex scenes
what_they_did: When a change in the captured lip image is detected, audio, lip-image and facial-EMG signals are captured synchronously, multi-source features are encoded by a speech model, and a language model synthesises text.
useful_for_us: Confirms the Chinese defence lab claims lip image plus facial EMG plus audio fusion for noisy, private or vocal-cord-damaged scenarios; active, and a broad multimodal claim to check.

title: CN111190484B — Multimodal interaction system and method
what_they_did: An acquisition module collects EEG, EMG, lip images, eye images and physiological parameters; machine learning recognises commands, language and emotion, and an interaction module dispatches them.
useful_for_us: A very broad multimodal claim that sweeps in EEG plus EMG plus lip and eye images; even though we do not plan EEG, the breadth shows how much of the multimodal space this lab has claimed.

title: CN111899713A — Silent communication method, device and equipment and storage medium
what_they_did: Facial EMG, lip optical images and oral-cavity ultrasound images are acquired synchronously, preprocessed and feature-extracted for silent communication.
useful_for_us: A sensor-fusion dead-end to note: it needs an intraoral ultrasound probe, which cannot be hidden like a jaw patch, but it shows the lab explored ultrasound as an alternative to EMG.

title: CN113887339A — Silent speech recognition system and method fusing surface electromyogram signal and lip image
what_they_did: A surface-EMG acquisition and recognition pipeline is fused with a lip-image acquisition and preprocessing pipeline to recognise silent speech.
useful_for_us: Tianjin University's EMG-plus-lip fusion; the application is marked DISCONTINUED, which is useful evidence that fusing a camera with sEMG did not pay off and that pure sEMG is the leaner route.

title: CN111723717A — Silent speech recognition method and system
what_they_did: Facial EMG data and vocal-cord vibration data are acquired during speaking, preprocessed, feature-fused, and trained and recognised with deep learning to output a command result.
useful_for_us: Adds vocal-cord vibration to facial EMG; DISCONTINUED, so the two-sensor combination was tried and dropped, another signal that more sensors do not automatically help.

title: CN109745045A — Myoelectric electrode patch and silent voice recognition equipment
what_they_did: The patch stacks a flexible substrate, a first insulating layer, a flexible electrode layer with multiple electrode probes and interconnect wires, and a second insulating layer, and the probes collect myoelectric signals for silent-voice recognition equipment.
useful_for_us: A concrete flexible dry-electrode patch design from Soochow University; the application is DISCONTINUED, so the layered patch geometry itself is relatively free to reuse.

title: CN110996782B — In-ear potential sensor
what_they_did: An audio product has at least two electrodes, a processor and an electroacoustic transducer; a signal obtained through an electrode and affected by the user's action leads the processor to take an action controlling another device.
useful_for_us: Bose's in-ear biopotential electrode claim, active with a seven-member family (EP3668392, US10575777B2, WO2019036114A1); a direct watch-out for an earbud that senses electrical signals from the ear canal.

title: CN112424859B — Systems and methods for improved speech recognition using neuromuscular information
what_they_did: The Chinese counterpart of the Meta claim: multiple neuromuscular sensors on wearable devices record neuromuscular signals, and a trained inference model determines text from audio and the neuromuscular signals.
useful_for_us: Meta filed the same neuromuscular-plus-audio claim in China and it is active, so any China-based jaw EMG product faces the same claim there as in the US.

title: CN115705841A — Speech recognition using accelerometer sensing for bone conduction
what_they_did: An accelerometer senses vibrations of one or more bones and no audio input is used, yet voice-command and natural-language recognition are performed from the bone-conduction signal alone.
useful_for_us: STMicroelectronics claims accelerometer-only speech recognition with no microphone; its family (EP4131256A1, US12603087B2, US20230045064A1) is a direct watch-out for a jaw- or ear-mounted accelerometer picking up bone conduction.

title: JP7149492B2 — EMG-assisted communication device with context-sensitive user interface
what_they_did: An EMG-assisted communication device presents a context-sensitive user interface, using muscle signals to drive communication for users who cannot speak.
useful_for_us: Control Bionics' assistive EMG communication device, active with continuations US11284844B2 and US12455623B2; relevant prior art for the user-interface side of an EMG speech device rather than the sensor itself.

title: KR20250142168A — System and method for silent speech communication using the attachable optical sensor
what_they_did: An attachable optical sensor has an optical-fibre layer in a lattice structure, a support member and an optical receiver, and the system uses it for silent speech communication.
useful_for_us: ETRI's optical-fibre deformation route to silent speech, pending with a JP grant (JP7714768B1) and a US application; a non-EMG Korean competitor worth monitoring and a possible alternative sensing modality.

title: KR102270653B1 — Speech production and facial expression mapping system using articulatory physical properties
what_they_did: A sensor unit adjacent to one side of the speaker's head or neck measures the physical properties of the articulatory organs, including an oral-tongue sensor, and the system maps them to speech and facial expression data.
useful_for_us: Inha University claims articulatory (including tongue) sensing rather than EMG, inside a 34-member Korean family; shows Korean universities were building the same speech-production sensing space with different modalities.

title: DE102020110901B4 — Method for generating an artificial voice
what_they_did: Acoustic signals of healthy speakers reading a known text are recorded together with at least one vocal-tract signal of a patient articulating the same text, and an artificial voice is generated from the pairing.
useful_for_us: Altavo's vocal-tract sensing plus voice-synthesis claim, active with EP4139917 and US20230154450A1; the closest thing to a radar/ultrasound jaw-neck competitor and a strong watch-out in Europe.

title: JP6960189B2 — Vocalization device
what_they_did: A vocalisation device assigned to Suzhou Yichuan Electronic Technology, with an 11-member family spanning CN107820178B, EP3637797B1 and US11223897B2.
useful_for_us: A Chinese hardware company hold on a vocalisation device; less about decoding silent speech than about producing sound, but it shows the adjacent speaker/vocaliser patent thicket around the mouth and throat.

title: Development of sEMG sensors and algorithms for silent speech recognition
what_they_did: Builds surface-EMG sensors and recognition algorithms specifically for silent speech, reporting on electrode placement and classification of silently mouthed words.
useful_for_us: The clearest sensor-and-algorithm paper for our exact task, and the source of the electrode-placement practice we should copy before buying an amplifier.

title: Evaluation of a wireless wearable tongue-computer interface by individuals with high-level spinal cord injuries
what_they_did: Evaluates a wireless wearable tongue-computer interface with magnetic tracer tracking in users with high-level spinal cord injuries, reporting usability and performance.
useful_for_us: Demonstrates that an intraoral magnetic interface is wearable and clinically usable, so it is a serious alternative if our jaw EMG proves too noisy, but it needs a tongue tracer.

title: An arch-shaped intraoral tongue drive system with built-in tongue-computer interfacing electronics
what_they_did: Presents an arch-shaped intraoral device with built-in interfacing electronics for a tongue drive system, integrating the sensor array into a dental retainer form factor.
useful_for_us: A complete intraoral integration example; useful mainly as a contrast to the behind-ear/jaw form factor we want, since a retainer is not hidden from the wearer's own mouth feel.

title: Computerised system translates 'subvocal speech' into action
what_they_did: A short news report on NASA Ames' subvocal speech system, which used throat surface EMG to classify silently spoken words into control commands.
useful_for_us: The historical origin of subvocal EMG control; its date shows the idea is over twenty years old, which is useful for prior-art arguments even though it never became a product.

title: Can we decode phonetic features in inner speech using surface electromyography?
what_they_did: Tests whether phonetic features of inner speech can be decoded from surface EMG of the orofacial muscles, finding that some but not all articulatory features are recoverable.
useful_for_us: A careful negative-ish result that tells us exactly which phonetic dimensions survive in inner speech EMG and which do not, so we do not promise phoneme accuracy we cannot get.

title: Towards optimizing electrode configurations for silent speech recognition
what_they_did: Searches over surface-EMG electrode configurations for silent speech recognition and reports which channel placements and densities carry the most decoding information.
useful_for_us: Gives a starting electrode layout from the Chinese high-density sEMG group, saving us a full hardware search before we build the jaw patch.

title: Biosignal sensors and deep learning-based speech recognition: a review
what_they_did: Reviews biosignal sensors and deep-learning speech recognition, covering EMG, EEG and related modalities with their electrode types and reported accuracies.
useful_for_us: A single citation to compare sensor modalities and electrode types before committing to EMG, and a source of accuracy numbers to benchmark our own prototype against.

title: Prosodic preferences of surface electromyography-based subvocal speech for communication
what_they_did: Studies which prosodic patterns users can reliably produce and which the sEMG system can recover in subvocal speech for communication.
useful_for_us: Shows prosody is recoverable from subvocal sEMG, which matters if we want natural-sounding output rather than just command words.

title: Noninvasive speech restoration after total laryngectomy using surface electromyography
what_they_did: Applies surface EMG of the residual articulatory muscles to restore speech for total-laryngectomy patients, reporting a clinical restoration pipeline.
useful_for_us: Confirms the clinical pull for silent sEMG speech and gives the assessment protocol we could borrow when validating our own device on one user.

title: CochlearMotion: head gesture recognition leveraging ear canal deformation
what_they_did: Uses ear-canal deformation measured inside an earbud to recognise head gestures, showing the deformation signal is informative enough for machine learning.
useful_for_us: Direct evidence that in-ear deformation sensing works, so an earbud lead for our jaw device can double as a motion channel without adding a visible sensor.

title: Can LLMs understand unvoiced speech? Exploring EMG-to-text conversion with LLMs
what_they_did: Explores using large language models for EMG-to-text conversion of unvoiced speech, testing whether a language model can clean up noisy EMG decoding.
useful_for_us: Shows the current frontier is EMG-to-text with an LLM decoder, which is the cheapest way for us to get usable text out of a small personal sEMG corpus.

title: Digital voicing of silent speech
what_they_did: Voices silent speech by decoding surface EMG of the face during silently mouthed speech, with an accompanying public code release.
useful_for_us: A verified silent-EMG-to-speech result with released code, so it is both a baseline method and a reusable implementation to test on our own recordings.

title: emg2speech: synthesizing speech from electromyography using self-supervised learning
what_they_did: Synthesises speech from orofacial EMG using self-supervised learning, reducing the labelled-data requirement for EMG-to-speech.
useful_for_us: Self-supervision is exactly what a one-user project needs because labelled silent-speech data is expensive to record; this is the method to try first.

title: dgaddy/silent_speech: code for voicing silent speech from EMG
what_they_did: Official repository for the Digital Voicing of Silent Speech paper, containing the EMG-to-speech models and training code.
useful_for_us: Ready-to-run EMG-to-speech code we can adapt to our own jaw recordings instead of writing a decoder from scratch.

title: HarshavardhanaTG/emg2speech: converting orofacial surface EMG to speech
what_they_did: Public code release for the emg2speech self-supervised orofacial-EMG-to-speech work.
useful_for_us: A second reusable decoder, specifically self-supervised, which fits the small labelled dataset we will have as one user.

title: MAILAB-Yonsei/Silent-Speech-Interfaces
what_they_did: Yonsei University lab repository collecting silent-speech-interface code and experiments.
useful_for_us: A Korean lab's working code and configs, useful to compare preprocessing choices against the Chinese and US pipelines.

title: Surface EMG Dataset for Silent Speech Recognition
what_they_did: A public surface-EMG dataset recorded for silent speech recognition and released on figshare.
useful_for_us: A ready public sEMG corpus for silent speech, so we can pretrain or sanity-check our decoder before collecting our own jaw data.
